steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Place broccoli in a steamer over 1 inch boiling water. Cover and cook until crisp-tender, 2 to 6 minutes. Drain.

Melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add flour and stir, cooking until bubbly. Stir in onion, then milk. Bring to a boil and cook for 1 minute. Remove from heat and season with salt and pepper.
Add cheese and eggs and stir until cheese melts. Add broccoli and stir to coat. Transfer mixture to a 9x13-inch casserole dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbly, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Broccoli Cheese Bake
raw_recipe.description: This broccoli bake is a tasty breadcrumb-free twist on au gratin! Easily customizable, make it with skim milk, fat-free cheese, or with or without eggs.

review.reviewBody: I love this recipe! I did make a few modifications. Instead of swiss cheese, I used authentic gruyere. I substituted a few shallots for the onion, and added 1 tsp. of nutmeg to the sauce. I found it slightly on the saucy side, as opposed to firm, so I think next time I will add another couple of eggs. However, the basic structure of the recipe is wonderful - it lends itself perfectly to any adaptation. I prepared it the night before and put it in the fridge, and took it out half an hour before I baked it. My guests absolutely raved over it - I served it with a brunch, but it would go well with any meal.

Delicious. This is a great jumping off point but I made several modifications. (I know, I know. I hate people who leave reviews but alter the recipe- but hear me out! The method is solid but this recipe can be customized, dare I say Amplified with some additions!)
When adding the chopped onions I also threw in 3 minced garlic cloves at the same time. Used 2/3 cheddar cheese and 1/3 Gouda for the shredded cheese mix. When the onion/cheese/egg mixture was incorporated I added 1 Tbsp Paprika, 1 Tbsp Worcester sauce, 2 Tbsp stone ground Dijon mustard, onion powder, and garlic powder. Essentially I recreated my favorite Beer Cheese fondue recipe and created a Broccoli Beer Cheese Casserole! Beyond amazing. The entire pan was demolished. Will make again and again!
I used cheddar and jack cheese plus halved the recipe. Worked great in 8X8 casserole dish.
I made it in cupcake pans and they poofed up at the top... it was wonderful! I don't think I would add a single thing.

Steam cut and lightly salted broccoli in microwave using a freezer bag- don’t add liquid. Cook the onion in a little butter, then add additional butter and flour, make a roux with milk, and just omit the eggs. Add a tiny pinch of nutmeg and red pepper flake to taste. Add extra sharp cheddar with the Swiss, and top with crushed butter cracker crumbs, and 1/2 c. powdered Parmesan and paprika to make the top golden brown and delicious.

So I made a bunch of changes to try a lower fat/calorie, higher protein (w/some spice upgrades) version of this bake (note, this is not a vegetarian option): 
Okay, so here are my modifications:
Used only 3 TBSP butter, and sauteed onions until translucent/browned, then added just 4 TBSPs of alternative flour ( I used half oat and half almond ) to make paste, added 1 cup milk slowly to smooth out sauce, then stir in 1/3 cup non-fat greek yogurt. Then add lite jarlesberg cheese (only 5-6 oz), 2 TBSP mustard (whole grain, slightly spicy is best), 1 TBSP worcestershire sauce, as well as powdered garlic, ground nutmeg and s&p to taste; Lastly, stir in 6 oz of lean smoked ham, diced small; (all other ingredients and instructions are same); Sprinkled 1/3 cup grated parmesan and 2-3 TBSP wheat germ evenly across top of casserole. Cooked as recommended, but then cooked under broiler for additional 5-10 mins to crisp up topping. 

Here are the nutritional stats for this version:
Serving Size: 1 cup (makes 8 servings)
Calories: 200, 16g Protein, 11g Carbs, 4g Sugar, 10g Fat

I made a smaller version of this recipe (6 cups broccoli, 2 Tbsp. Butter, 1 Tbsp. Flour, half an onion, 2 cups cheese, 1 cup of 1% milk, 1 egg) and it came out wonderfully. We served it at a dinner for four and still had almost half of it left over.

I'm living outside the US and far from lots of the canned products used in many Thanksgiving recipes. This recipe is creamy, cheesy and easy to make. I found it to be a great substitute for the cream of mushroom broccoli casserole my mom makes. I added sauteed mushrooms to my dish and some garlic to boost the flavors. Next time I made include a bit of chicken stock too.

Good recipe. We're doing low carb so I substituted the AP flour for Soy flour and it worked great to thicken it and bring it all together. Also, used 1/2 cup whole milk and 1/2 cup half/half to cut out a few more carbs.

Next time I will saute the onions before adding them to the butter for another depth. Overall it's a good recipe and I will make again!

I like this recipe. Cook it several times, but I adjusted a little bit by eliminating egg and adding Parmesann cheese on top, as well as increase the temperature to 390 degrees about the last 10 minutes to make it looks brown. (it can be less than 10 minutes, keep watching it! :)) 
I prefer to have the taste of cheeses. 
The sweetness of Swiss cheese and sweet onion make this recipe taste great. My husband really like it.

This was really good.. I used Ritz crackers on top.. I added 3/4 can of milk and one egg to the cream of mushroom soup and baked 25 min.. I love love love it.. I did use broccoli florets also.. mine was not bland like some reviews have mentioned.. I seasoned my chicken very well (I added this to the recipe) and seasoned the water for the broccoli!! Will definitely make again

This was a nice and easy side dish I helped make, we added some other staple seasonings for our household, didn’t have Swiss so used 2 cups medium cheddar and 2 cups of a fiesta blend we had. Super tasty.
Easy, quick, Everybody happy.........................making lots to freeze, thank you.......
I changed some ingredients instead of flour I used progresso crumbs 1 egg 1 can Carnation milk Two different cheeses to my liking Velveeta etc

Loved this recipe. It is easy. But I have made my fair share of rioux. The trick is to continuously whisk while heating when adding flour, milk, eggs, cheese, etc and being sure not to overheat. I omitted the onion and added fresh garden thyme and smoked paprika to the milk simmer and used aged white cheddar. Easy to experiment with different cheeses and milks. This is a real gooey baked dish which is perfect for those who need a little help with digesting broccoli or need a healthy high fat meal that is easy to chew. I added finely chopped walnuts after cooking and broiled for 2 minutes. Delicious with some mashed potatoes or wild rice, field peas and mushroom gravy. Good home cooked winter meal.

The recipe was easy, even with needing to temper the egg before adding it to the white sauce, and it cooked up just beautifully. I will be altering the amount of onion in future. I don't know whether my small onion wasn't small enough or whether I just prefer a purer taste of vegetables, in this case broccoli, but even with using a sweet Vidalia onion, it was overpowering. I think replacing the onion with more broccoli will maintain the body of the casserole. Thanks for the recipe!
Yummy but I tweaked it. I had 2 cups of cheese (used colliers welsh cheddar) added half a cup of cream cheese and about 2 cups of milk and an extra egg. Family loved it.

Used Gruyere bc I've been in such a rut with Cheddar. The G cheese has a fabulous taste. Made 1/2 recipe. I chopped the broccoli into 1' pieces and microwaved with the chopped onion until crisp tender. Incorporated the sauce and broccoli thoroughly. Love this.

Turned out wonderfully fluffy, thanks for sharing, that was new style of bake for me! I remember now I saw a video with Julia Child explaining French Broccoli soufflé using the same base- bechamel sauce and eggs. Very tasty!
